name: ABS
description: ABS returns the absolute value of a number, removing the negative sign if present.
tldr: ABS converts negative numbers to positive, leaving positive numbers unchanged.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The number for which you want the absolute value.

basicExample.description: Get absolute value of a number
basicExample.explanation: Converts -10 to its absolute value of 10.

advancedExamples.title: Calculate absolute differences
advancedExamples.description: Find the absolute difference between two values
advancedExamples.explanation: Returns the positive difference regardless of which value is larger.

advancedExamples.title: Sum absolute values
advancedExamples.description: Sum all absolute values in a range
advancedExamples.explanation: Converts all values to positive before summing.

howItWorks: ABS removes the negative sign from negative numbers, returning their positive equivalent. Positive numbers and zero remain unchanged.

howToSteps.name: Select output cell
howToSteps.text: Choose where the result should appear.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The result shows the absolute value.

limitations: ABS only works with numeric values.
For array operations, use ABS with array formulas or dynamic arrays.

commonErrors.fix: Ensure the argument is a number.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ABS works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: Does ABS work with arrays?
faq.answer: In Excel 365 and Google Sheets, ABS works with arrays natively. In older versions, use array formulas (Ctrl+Shift+Enter).
